g.aria-description:
This scene graph is static and read-only. Do not try to highlight, create selectable regions on, or act on any part of it.
This diagram shows a debugging fix: a buggy program and its corrected version, each paired with the grid state after the first repetition of its loop.
Buggy program: - repeat 4 times (desaturated) - drive forward (desaturated) - deliver package (desaturated) - turn right - drive forward
Fixed program: - repeat 4 times (desaturated) - drive forward (desaturated) - deliver package (desaturated) - drive forward - turn right
The two programs differ in the order of the last two steps in the loop body: the buggy program turns right before driving forward, while the fixed program drives forward before turning right.
Legend: ✓ = completed delivery, X = uncompleted delivery, C = the truck (shown only when it's on an intersection with no delivery), . = intersection with no delivery. If the truck ends on a completed delivery, that cell shows ✓ (not C) and the truck's position is given in the description. Grids are written top row = north.
Both programs run on the same 3x3 grid of intersections (2x2 blocks) with 4 deliveries. The truck started at the bottom-left intersection facing north. Starting configuration: .X. X.X CX.
Map for the buggy program (state shown is after the first repetition): the truck drove forward to the middle-left intersection and delivered that package, then turned right to face east and drove forward to the center intersection, where it ended facing east. One delivery was completed; the truck is now in the middle of the grid, off the perimeter. .X. ✓CX .X.
Map for the fixed program (state shown is after the first repetition): the truck drove forward to the middle-left intersection and delivered that package, then drove forward again to the top-left intersection and turned right to face east, where it ended facing east. One delivery was completed; the truck stayed on the perimeter. CX. ✓.X .X.
